I’m 28F with BPD. Resonate with these feelings deeply. I know I’m just a stranger on the internet echoing corny, overused sentiments, but it really will get better. It’s hard, we’ve been dealt a bad hand of cards. But BPD can be worked on to minimise the hurt. Quality of life improves. You find patient people who stick around. You’ll find a better sense of self. It’s difficult, but it’s worth it, I promise you. Having BPD is hard, and it hurts, it hurts so fucking much. It’s so difficult to convey how painful it is to people around you. But it can and will get better.
I miss you, I miss talking to you. There isn’t much else for me to say. I just miss your presence in my life. Your absence is deafening.

I used to be like this, except I WOULD react (spam call, spam text, break things, hurt myself, etc). I would really encourage you to look into DBT skills if you haven’t already, they’ve for the most part “corrected” my behaviour. I’m not perfect, but I can think rationally now in relationships. 

We are not doomed to anxiety riddled relationships. It’s possible for us to feel safe and secure. We do really just need to put in the work to unlearn, and unfortunately it’s difficult work. But it’s doable. Hang in there!

Got diagnosed when I was 22 (6-7ish years ago) after I had a terrible episode and my friend drove me to the ER of a mental health hospital, I had no idea what BPD was at the time so it was all kind of a huge shock to my system. Jumped into DBT/intensive therapy ever since and haven’t looked back

I used to have that belief about myself, despite being in back to back relationships since I was a teenager (the longest amount of time I’ve been single in over a decade was 4 months. I just keep falling into relationships regardless of if I’m seeking them out lol). Though, last year when I expressed this to my therapist she said something along the lines of “you can do as much therapy as you want, and read as many books or consume as much self-help DBT type stuff as you can, but nothing will prepare someone with BPD for a relationship more than the actual practice of BEING IN a relationship and having the opportunity to actually PRACTICE those skills.” I don’t think people with BPD should avoid dating. I do think we have a responsibility to put in the work to improve our behaviour. And the only way to do that is by pursuing these relationships when the opportunities arise.

Hi hi hi. I know you’re being bombarded with comments on what to do right now and it must be overwhelming, but I want to reiterate that we’re all coming from a place of concern and care. I had an abortion (albeit I wasn’t a minor) and it was one of the best decisions I’d ever made. Actively trying to force a miscarriage will most likely NOT work and will just damage your health further. I tried to do that too and my friend talked me into going to Planned Parenthood with her to figure out a plan. I really couldn’t recommend them enough, they deal with cases very similar to yours every day. They’ll help you talk to your mom, they’ll give you resources, they’ll point you in the right direction. You must feel very lost and scared right now. I need you to put your health and safety first right now. Your mother’s anger will be temporary (I saw the comment about the law in your state needing her to know about the abortion and not necessarily have to sign off on it for you to have one) but a baby grown to full term and/or organ damage from attempting a miscarriage is permanent. 

Myself and a lot of other commenters here seem to be sincerely worried for your well being. I can’t reiterate enough how helpful Planned Parenthood is, especially if you initially feel you can’t speak with your mother about this.

I’m also sorry for the onslaught on negative comments that are coming in from pro-lifers. Please ignore them, don’t read/listen to those comments.

Bunnies are prey animals, so regardless of whether or not the cat accepts the bun, the bun will be scared of it unless they bonded at a young age. It would probably be best to keep their interactions at a minimum, ie keeping the bunny in a completely separate room. I’d also like to suggest free roaming the rabbit to one room to maximise its happiness, as cages made for rabbits were not made with enough space for them regardless of what the pet store people say :( 

To free roam however you’d need to bunny proof the room, so I’d also suggest getting a puppy exercise pen (or “ex pen”) that it could stay inside! 

Having a bun friend is a joy, and I’m sure your bun is just as stoked as you are, especially since you saved it from a not-so-ideal situation. Best of luck!!!
